name: cdn-cache-invalidation-p1
prompt: how do I serve assets from the edge but still push out an update instantly when a file changes

chunks.content: kickoff: the marketing site feels slow from Asia, goal this sprint is to cut time-to-first-byte for static content
user sessions are cached in memory for the request lifetime so we do not refetch the profile on every handler
the image pipeline produces webp and avif variants and picks one based on the Accept header
the expensive leaderboard query result is cached for sixty seconds so we do not recompute it on every page view
enabled brotli compression on text responses, shaving roughly 70 percent off CSS and JS payloads
lowered the DNS TTL to 300 seconds ahead of the provider migration so cutover is fast
added a robots.txt disallowing the staging subdomain from being indexed
each built asset gets a content-hash in its filename, so a changed file is a brand new URL and the edge never serves a stale copy
hashed asset URLs are served with a far-future max-age marked immutable, while the HTML that references them stays uncacheable so new hashes propagate immediately
for the rare un-hashed file we call the edge provider's purge API on deploy to evict that exact path right away
turned on an origin shield layer so a cold edge node fetches from a regional cache instead of hammering the origin
narrowed the third-party OAuth scopes to read-only after a security review
a nightly cron purges soft-deleted rows older than 30 days
added type hints across the billing module and turned on mypy strict for that package
accessibility audit flagged missing alt text on hero images, now fixed
